sonnet.q1: The gateway returns 401 Unauthorized. No counter is read or changed.
sonnet.q2: All of a customer's keys share one budget (key is by customer ID), so in total the plan limit per minute: 100/min for Standard (up to about 200 across a minute boundary). Enterprise has no limit set yet.
sonnet.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (seconds). The backend never sees the request; it is not forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. A denied request leaves the count unchanged and uses no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The count is increased before forwarding, so a backend failure (including 500) still uses budget.
sonnet.q6: No retry. The gateway fails open: it forwards the request to the backend right away, emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, and the client gets the backend's response without X-RateLimit headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: read from configuration, no value set yet, so Enterprise requests are currently not rate-limited.
sonnet.q8: In one shared Redis counter store, under key rl:{customerId}:{epochMinute}. A TTL of about 120 seconds, set on first use, makes Redis delete old keys automatically.
sonnet.q9: When the next fixed one-minute clock-aligned window starts: a new epoch minute means a new key, so the count starts from zero. The old key expires via TTL.
sonnet.q10: A Lua script runs in Redis as one atomic step (check and increment together). No other command runs in the middle, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: Seconds until the current window ends, rounded up, minimum 1 (e.g. 15 at second 45). The Lua script computes it from Redis TIME, so gateway clock skew does not matter. The gateway copies it into the header.
sonnet.q12: No retry. The client gets the backend's response with no X-RateLimit headers (no limit or remaining info), since the count is unknown.
